topic: Exact three-arm face/corner second-order minimax constant and allocation frontier for binary finite-population contrasts. For arbitrary binary complete schedules and every assignment law independent of them, compare unrestricted minimax squared-error risk with iid q*=(1/2,1/4,1/4) for contrast (1,-1/2,-1/2). Prove both deficits from 1/n converge after n^(4/3) scaling to the same explicit Airy constant; derive the arm-labelled stratified face/corner decision experiment from the exact eight-type orbit game; and construct matching finite-n estimators and complete-schedule priors. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: the eight-type tangent program yields V(theta,eta)=max(|theta|/2,|eta|/4), a half-wedge Airy operator, a label-preserving half-effect prior, and an allocation-regularizing broad-prior mixture; exact arithmetic reproduces the n=3 label gap. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: close the singular eta=0 experiment and finite-orbit bridge with uniform upper/lower remainders. EARLY KILL TEST: verify the posterior-target coefficient and uniform allocation square completion. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_threearm_facecorner_sharp_constant.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For the binary three-arm contrast (1,-1/2,-1/2), do unrestricted schedule-independent assignment and iid assignment at q*=(1/2,1/4,1/4) have the same explicit n^(-4/3) Airy correction to minimax squared-error risk?

source_refs.claim: The two-arm binary finite-population problem has an unrestricted minimax expansion 1/n-C_A n^(-4/3)+o(n^(-4/3)) obtained from a one-dimensional Airy problem.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Provides finite-population estimation theory for arbitrary multi-treatment contrasts and unequal replications, but not unrestricted nonlinear minimax risk or sharp second-order constants.
source_refs.author: Rahul Mukerjee, Tirthankar Dasgupta, Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: without imposing overlap and without asserting an elementary closed-form classification.
every response orbit in the positive support of the least-favorable prior has primal risk exactly v

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published sharp minimax reduction is two-arm: four schedule types collapse to a scalar shifted-binomial experiment and a one-dimensional Airy operator. Three binary potential outcomes instead produce eight labelled types, two tangent coordinates, intersecting face and corner regimes, and a singular axis. The prior CausalSmith construction proves finite orbit-game existence and complementary slackness but explicitly stops before a closed-form classification and supplies no explicit asymptotically least-favorable prior. The missing work is a uniform local reduction, an arm-labelled half-wedge spectral problem, and matching upper and lower expansions over every schedule-independent assignment law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact eight-type decision reduction and an explicit constant C_3 proving R_n^all=1/n-C_3 n^(-4/3)+o(n^(-4/3)) and R_n^iid(q*)=1/n-C_3 n^(-4/3)+o(n^(-4/3)), with matching finite-n estimators and complete-schedule priors.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation connects joint design-estimator minimaxity, an exact finite experiment, and a practically meaningful sharp second-order comparison.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimize design and estimator jointly -> standard procedures are only first-order minimax -> reduce binary schedules to a finite decision problem -> derive the sharp correction for a labelled three-arm contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Orbit reduction, nonlinear score shrinkage, a discrete Stein identity for the upper bound, and discretized squared-eigenfunction priors with Van Trees control for the lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the desired form of sharp minimax expansion on a scalar two-arm tangent space; the proposed result must replace its line geometry and symmetric prior by labelled half-wedge analogues.

method_exemplars.technique: Second-order asymptotic minimax analysis through square completion and the positive ground state of a problem-specific differential operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired constant is likewise a ground-state value, but on a singular domain with a face and corner.

method_exemplars.technique: Arm-labelled representation of general finite-population contrasts under arbitrary assignment probabilities and unequal replications.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its multi-treatment bookkeeping supplies the outer design-based framework for the eight schedule types and the allocation q*.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the singular eta=0 boundary of the three-arm face/corner experiment be closed uniformly without discarding zero-likelihood posterior cells or dormant finite-game risk constraints?

source_refs.excerpt: zero-likelihood cells may take any clipped value

open_problems.why_unsolved: The finite orbit proof can assign an arbitrary clipped posterior version on a null cell while retaining feasibility constraints for response orbits outside the prior support. At eta=0 this bookkeeping becomes load-bearing: convergence away from the boundary does not establish that omitted likelihood ratios, arbitrary versions, and dormant primal constraints induce the proposed half-wedge experiment. The first missing step is a uniform deficiency or direct risk comparison across positive-likelihood and null cells, with an explicit treatment of the singular posterior-target coefficient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform experiment-convergence or risk-comparison theorem on |eta|<=epsilon_n, including eta=0, with explicit o(n^(-4/3)) remainders and a boundary decision rule preserving every finite-game primal constraint.

writing_exemplar.why: Its reduction makes the boundary layer itself the statistical source of the second-order gain, providing the closest framing for why a singular subexperiment cannot be ignored.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Worst-case schedules concentrate near a variance boundary -> local observations converge to a nonregular experiment -> the spectral boundary problem controls minimax risk -> establish the corresponding limit uniformly at the three-arm singular axis.

method_exemplars.technique: Uniform lattice-to-diffusion risk expansion and matching discretized least-favorable priors near a binary boundary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same upper/lower comparison is required, but it must remain valid where one coordinate and some posterior cells disappear.

method_exemplars.technique: Local asymptotic minimax lower bounds expressed through a limiting differential operator and its positive ground state.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the operator-based comparison that must be extended to the half-wedge boundary condition.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp local allocation frontier around q*=(1/2,1/4,1/4): which arm-labelled triangular arrays q_n retain the optimal Airy correction, and what explicit second-order penalty applies outside that set?

source_refs.claim: Under permutation-invariant outcome classes and linear estimation, optimal treatment counts obey a first-order Neyman-allocation principle.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.claim: In the balanced two-arm problem, the n^(-4/3) gain arises from an n^(2/3) boundary layer and nonlinear shrinkage at that scale.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Develops design-based multi-arm asymptotics under fixed limiting allocation proportions, without a nonregular local minimax allocation frontier.
source_refs.author: Anqi Zhao, Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.excerpt: the common-probability independent designs form a subclass of the unrestricted designs

open_problems.why_unsolved: First-order Neyman allocation identifies q* from the absolute contrast weights but discards local allocation losses that can compete with an n^(-4/3) shrinkage gain. The two-arm Airy analysis has no allocation simplex, while standard multi-arm asymptotics keep allocation proportions fixed away from its boundary. The prior finite polynomial comparison is exact but has not been expanded uniformly along n-dependent labelled perturbations. The missing argument is a joint square completion over posterior cells, schedule-type counts, and q_n, including face sequences where an arm probability becomes locally sparse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient scaling characterization q_n=q*+r_n h and an explicit frontier functional F(h) such that the n^(4/3)-scaled risk correction equals the unrestricted constant precisely on a stated set of h and incurs penalty F(h)>0 outside it.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates unequal replication through the concrete task of estimating a specified multi-treatment finite-population contrast.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Multi-arm experiments target weighted contrasts -> assignment shares determine first-order precision -> nearby allocations remain indistinguishable at first order -> a sharp local frontier must separate them.

method_exemplars.technique: Permutation symmetrization and minimax quadratic optimization yielding Neyman allocation and its optimal linear estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the first-order allocation square completion whose remainder must be retained and coupled to the Airy layer.

method_exemplars.technique: Boundary-layer risk scaling, Riccati-derived nonlinear shrinkage, and uniform control of lattice remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired frontier is governed by competition between allocation loss and this n^(-4/3) shrinkage gain.

method_exemplars.technique: Vectorization of arm means and contrasts with finite-population expansions under multi-arm complete randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its labelled covariance bookkeeping can carry q_n perturbations before the nonregular correction is introduced.

open_problems.open_problem: Under fixed-count three-arm complete randomization at counts nearest nq*, does conditioning away allocation-count randomness preserve, reduce, or eliminate the half-wedge Airy improvement for the unrestricted minimax estimator?

source_refs.claim: Shows complete randomization is strictly worse than independent randomization for a broad affine class with bounded outcomes and leaves strict suboptimality under arbitrary estimators as a conjecture.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: For two arms, complete randomization with difference-in-means has worst-case risk 1/(n-1), while independent randomization with nonlinear shrinkage has a negative n^(-4/3) correction.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known strict comparison is limited to an affine or equivariant estimator class, with unrestricted-estimator strictness still conjectural. In three arms, conditioning on exact arm counts replaces the product experiment by coupled labelled hypergeometric counts; this removes the realized-share statistic used by midpoint-centered rules but may retain nonlinear information in the remaining orbit. Ordinary finite-population CLTs cannot distinguish alternatives at the n^(-4/3) risk scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact fixed-count orbit-game characterization and a uniform expansion R_n^CRE=1/n-C_CRE n^(-4/3)+o(n^(-4/3)), with an explicit C_CRE and a proof that it is smaller than, equal to, or zero relative to the iid-q* constant.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central narrative directly questions the conventional claim that fixing treatment counts must improve precision when potential outcomes have known support.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact balance is conventionally efficiency-improving -> bounded outcomes make realized shares informative -> independent assignment can outperform fixed counts -> determine the unrestricted three-arm second-order cost of conditioning.

method_exemplars.technique: Endpoint adversaries, midpoint-centered Horvitz-Thompson regression, and finite-dimensional quadratic programs for minimax estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These tools isolate at finite n which information is lost by conditioning on treatment counts.

method_exemplars.technique: Exact minimax duality, nonlinear posterior-mean rules, and Airy upper and lower expansions for bounded binary schedules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination asks whether the same mechanism survives after replacing the independent likelihood by a labelled hypergeometric orbit experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Finite-population combinatorial central limit theory for multiple treatment levels under complete randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the natural approximation machinery for fixed-count multi-arm designs, although it must be sharpened to uniform second-order risk control.

open_problems.open_problem: For three-arm potential outcomes in a known interval [L,U], is the unrestricted minimax contrast problem exactly reducible to endpoint-valued eight-type schedules, so that the binary half-wedge constant transfers after multiplication by (U-L)^2?

source_refs.claim: Extends the two-arm binary minimax value to arbitrary bounded potential outcomes through randomized endpoint representation and conditional expectation.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: In the two-arm bounded-outcome problem, least-favorable priors can be supported at potential-outcome endpoints and optimal nonlinear estimators arise from finite convex programs.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: For bounded finite-population totals under design-unbiased estimation, proves sharp endpoint-based minimax bounds and characterizes pairwise-independent inclusion designs.
source_refs.author: P. M. Aronow, Patrick Lopatto

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two-arm endpoint-randomization argument preserves a scalar transformed observation. With three mutually exclusive arm indicators and unequal contrast coefficients, coordinatewise endpoint randomization need not preserve the labelled sufficient orbit or the posterior-target coefficient after conditioning. No located result proves that the necessary Rao-Blackwell map remains risk-contracting for unrestricted multi-arm minimax estimation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-n equality between minimax risk over [L,U]^(3n) and (U-L)^2 times the binary eight-type risk, with an explicit conditional endpoint estimator and least-favorable prior, or a counterexample identifying the first n and labelled orbit where the reduction fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames known outcome support as actionable design information and makes endpoint geometry central to both estimator construction and lower bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome bounds change optimal randomization -> endpoint schedules are least favorable in two arms -> nonlinear estimators exploit the support -> determine whether endpoint reduction survives a labelled three-arm contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Randomized endpoint decomposition followed by conditional expectation of the binary minimax rule without increasing risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem is precisely the multi-arm validity or failure of this reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Least-favorable endpoint priors and a quadratic-constraint convex program producing a posterior-mean nonlinear estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An eight-type extension would provide the required finite-n estimator and prior pair.

method_exemplars.technique: Sharp rectangular-parameter-space lower bounds using endpoint sign patterns aligned with assignment dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same endpoint-adversary geometry can expose any multi-arm dependence obstruction missed by the two-arm reduction.

literature_map:
1. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2608.13822) provide the closest anchor: unrestricted two-arm binary finite-population minimax risk has an explicit Airy n^(-4/3) correction.
2. Their reduction uses four potential-outcome types, a scalar shifted-binomial experiment, nonlinear shrinkage, and discretized Airy-squared least-favorable priors.
3. The same paper treats bounded two-arm outcomes by endpoint randomization but does not analyze three or more treatment arms.
4. Hull (2026, arXiv:2608.09812) independently studies the two-arm bounded-outcome optimum and emphasizes that random realized treatment shares carry information.
5. Hull proves independent assignment beats complete randomization for broad affine estimators and leaves unrestricted-estimator strict suboptimality as a conjecture.
6. Bai (2023, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.10.009) derives complete randomization, linear estimation, and Neyman allocation under permutation-invariant classes, supplying a first-order benchmark.
7. Kallus (2018, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12240) develops minimax-variance designs and shows that balance gains require outcome-class structure.
8. Kallus (2021, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12412) separates minimax precision from assignment support needed for design-based testing but remains two-arm and variance-focused.
9. Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2017.1294076) provide the general framework for multi-treatment finite-population contrasts and unequal replications.
10. Li and Ding (2017/2018, JASA, arXiv:1610.04821) establish multi-treatment finite-population CLTs useful for regular fixed-count regimes but not the singular n^(-4/3) layer.
11. Zhao and Ding (2023, JRSSB, arXiv:2112.10557) develop multi-arm regression-adjustment asymptotics with fixed limiting allocations, without unrestricted minimax frontiers.
12. Aronow and Lopatto (2026, arXiv:2605.20572) show how bounded-support endpoint adversaries and pairwise-independent sampling yield exact minimax results for finite-population totals.
13. Bickel (1981, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/AOS/1176345646) and Levit (1981, Theory of Probability and Its Applications, DOI 10.1137/1125066) are classical anchors for second-order minimax constants via least-favorable priors and differential operators.
14. Targeted searches found multi-arm variance, regression, covariate-balance, and best-arm-regret work, but no three-arm fixed-schedule unrestricted-MSE result with an Airy constant, eight-type orbit reduction, or face/corner allocation frontier.
